Definition: probably from an obsolete σκέρπω (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting):--scorpion.
BiblicalUsage: Skorpios is the scorpion, and it stings in the hands of the enemy and in the tail of the locusts. Jesus gives His disciples power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and the locusts of the vision have tails like scorpions, with stings to hurt men five months.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the scorpion's sting is real but the authority over it is greater, because the Lord who gives power to tread on scorpions has already crushed the serpent.
